name: redex
why: Bytecode optimizer for Android apps, a real look inside how shipped Dalvik code is rewritten.

brief.what_it_is: Redex is an Android bytecode optimizer that works on .dex files, the compiled bytecode inside an APK. It provides a framework for reading, writing, and analyzing .dex files, plus a set of optimization passes built on that framework. The stated output is an APK that is smaller and faster than its source. The homepage describes Buck integration, where the Redex config is passed as a parameter to the Buck android_binary rule when the APK is generated. I did not see the input and output file formats or any command-line usage in the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The author frames it as a way to shrink and speed up Android apps: fewer bytes means faster downloads, faster installs, and lower data usage for cell users, and less bytecode typically means faster runtime performance. The README says it was originally developed at Facebook.
brief.how_it_works: The README says Redex has a framework for reading, writing, and analyzing dex files and uses that framework to run optimization passes that rewrite the bytecode. I did not find a more detailed explanation of the passes or their mechanism in the pages I read.
brief.install_notes: The pages I read give no install steps, runtime requirements, or first-run configuration. The homepage Getting Started page is a placeholder that says only: Hi, Redex is an Android bytecode optimizer and stuff. The one concrete integration described is Buck: the Redex config is passed to the Buck android_binary rule. The brew metadata lists an executable named redex.py, but I did not see it referenced in the README or docs, so I have not described how it is invoked.
brief.standout: Redex rewrites the bytecode of already-built APKs, which is a different niche from shrinking resources or code at build time. Its documented integration point is Buck, not Gradle, which is unusual for an Android tool.
brief.status: unknown. The README is short and links to the homepage for full documentation. I saw no release date, last-commit date, or version number in any page I fetched. The repository is public under the facebook organization and carries an MIT license with a CONTRIBUTING file, but I could not confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The documentation I could reach is very thin: the Getting Started page is a placeholder and there are no commands, examples, or platform details. I could not confirm which Android build systems besides Buck are supported. Nothing in the pages I read warns about stability or platform limits. The README does not say whether it is still actively maintained.
quotes: Redex provides a framework for reading, writing, and analyzing .dex files, and a set of optimization passes that use this framework to improve the bytecode.
An APK optimized by ReDex should be smaller and faster than its source.
